jobs.title: Security Engineer
jobs.description:
Security Engineer

About Boltz

Boltz is a public benefit company building the next generation of AI-powered molecular modeling tools to make biology programmable and accelerate drug discovery, while keeping frontier capabilities broadly accessible.

Boltz was founded by former MIT scientists who created Boltz-1, the first fully commercially available open-source model to approach AlphaFold 3-level accuracy in predicting the 3D structure of biomolecular complexes.

We focus on two things:

  • Foundation models. Our open models, Boltz-1, Boltz-2 and BoltzGen, are trusted by 100,000+ scientists across biotech and academia, and used in programs at every Top 20 pharma as well as leading agrichemical and industrial research organizations. Our latest proprietary foundation models power our products and the custom models we build with partners.

  • Boltz Lab and the Boltz API. Our products run our latest models, design pipelines (BoltzMol for small molecules, BoltzProt for protein design) and agents as reliable, production-grade tools built around real chemistry and biology workflows. Teams start from a target and a hypothesis, then generate, evaluate, and rank candidate molecules in Boltz Lab, run our models from their own code and agents through the Boltz API, or deploy them inside their own environment.

The two feed each other: our open releases earn scientific credibility and community insight, and our products turn our full range of models into real impact for partners including Pfizer, Takeda, GSK, Bristol Myers Squibb and DSM-Firmenich.

You can read more about our mission, research and product vision in our manifesto.

About the role

Our partners trust us with their most valuable secrets: unpublished targets, novel molecules and years of proprietary assay data. Your job is to make sure that trust is well placed, everywhere our platform runs: our own cloud, dedicated single-tenant environments, and partners' own AWS and Google Cloud accounts.

You will be a founding engineer on our security team, part of the Platform team in Core Engineering, shaping the security program with our CTO, who leads it today. You will work with every engineering team at Boltz, and you will sit across the table from the security leaders of the world's largest pharma companies.

We want security to be the reason a partner says yes faster, not the reason a deal stalls. This role is ideal for a hands-on engineer who would rather fix a control in code than write a document about it, and who can explain risk clearly to a pharma CISO.

What you'll do

  • Make secure the default: build guardrails into our Terraform, Kubernetes and CI/CD so every new cluster, environment and partner deployment inherits the right boundaries from day one.

  • Protect what matters most: keep partner data isolated across tenants and deployments, protect our model weights, and make sure the agents acting on scientists' behalf can only do what they should.

  • Make the secure path the easy path: identity, secrets, service-to-service authentication and supply-chain controls that engineers actually want to use.

  • See and stop threats: logging, detection and incident response across AWS and GCP, with exercises that keep us sharp.

  • Find weaknesses first: threat-model new features before they ship, run penetration tests, and attack our own agents and APIs before anyone else does.

  • Turn trust into an advantage: lead security reviews with partners' security teams, translate their requirements into engineering work early, and run our SOC 2 Type II program and the frameworks partners ask for next (e.g. ISO 27001) with evidence generated by our systems, not by screenshots.

  • Secure the company: identity, device management, access reviews and security awareness for a small, highly technical team.

This role is not a compliance-only (GRC) or SOC analyst role. Most of your time goes into engineering; compliance should be a by-product of controls that actually work.

About you

Minimum Requirements

  • 4+ years of security engineering experience in cloud-native SaaS or infrastructure companies.

  • Deep, hands-on cloud security experience on AWS or Google Cloud: IAM and multi-account or multi-project organizations, network security, encryption and key management, audit logging and threat detection.

  • Infrastructure-as-code (Terraform) and enough hands-on engineering to ship security improvements yourself.

  • Application security experience: threat modeling, secure code review, authentication and authorization (SSO, OAuth/OIDC, MFA), web and API vulnerabilities.

  • Experience owning a SOC 2 or ISO 27001 program through an external audit, or building the controls one depends on.

  • Practical incident response experience.

  • Low ego, high ownership, and pragmatic trade-offs between risk and speed; clear with engineers, leadership and partners' security teams alike.

Preferred Requirements

  • Kubernetes and container security (network policy, admission control, workload identity, image signing).

  • Security for ML or LLM systems: agent tool access, prompt injection, model and training-data protection.

  • Experience as an early or founding security hire at a startup.

  • Securing deployments in customer-controlled, multi-cloud or regulated environments.

jobs.description:
Ingénieur ou post-doctorant pour l'analyse des données acquises par un radar HF océanographique couvrant le Raz Blanchard

ENSTA, établissement d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche sous tutelle du ministère des Armées, développe des activités de formation, de recherche et d’innovation dans les domaines de la défense et de la sécurité, des transports, de l'énergie, des activités maritimes, du numérique et de la santé.

L’école, présente sur deux campus, à Paris-Saclay et à Brest, est membre de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Classée dans le Top 10 des meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France, elle a pour mission :

  • la formation d’élèves ingénieurs civils et militaires, de cadres et docteurs pour les secteurs public et privé,

  • la recherche et l’innovation de haut niveau en relation étroite avec l’industrie des grands secteurs de souveraineté au sein de 6 unités de formation et de recherche (UFR).

Le/la titulaire du poste sera affecté au sein de l’UFR S2I sur le Campus de Brest.

 

Projet FLOWATT

Le projet FLOWATT, dans le cadre duquel s’inscrit cette étude, vise à déployer et exploiter six hydroliennes dans les forts courants marins du Raz Blanchard, en Normandie.

Au-delà de la production d’énergie, FLOWATT a pour objectif d’évaluer le potentiel du Raz Blanchard pour le déploiement de fermes hydroliennes à plus grande échelle. Cette évaluation repose notamment sur une caractérisation précise de la ressource, une estimation fine du productible et une meilleure compréhension des impacts environnementaux. Pour répondre à ces enjeux, le projet combine mesures in situ, modélisation numérique et essais expérimentaux afin de fournir les connaissances nécessaires à la préparation des futurs déploiements commerciaux, tout en contribuant à la réduction des coûts de production et à la limitation des impacts sur l’environnement marin.

Dans ce contexte, la caractérisation de l’état de mer constitue un enjeu important, notamment dans une zone soumise à des courants très intenses. La présente étude s’intéresse ainsi aux données de radar HF acquises depuis fin 2017, ainsi qu’à celles qui seront nouvellement enregistrées dans le cadre du projet TidalRace. Le système, de technologie WERA, est réparti sur deux sites distants d’environ 5 km au Cap de la Hague et fonctionne à deux fréquences, 13,5 MHz et 24,5 MHz. Les acquisitions sont réalisées en continu, à raison de quatre mesures par heure, 24 h/24 et 7 j/7, sur une emprise couvrant l’ensemble du Raz Blanchard. Cette couverture temporelle et spatiale offre ainsi une opportunité unique de suivre l’évolution des états de mer dans des conditions hydrodynamiques particulièrement contraintes.

L’exploitation de ces données nécessite toutefois d’adapter les méthodes de traitement aux conditions de forts courants. L’objectif des travaux est donc d’améliorer les algorithmes existants et, si nécessaire, d’en développer de nouveaux afin de restituer de manière fiable les spectres d’énergie des vagues en fréquence et en direction, ainsi que les paramètres moyens associés. Une première étape consistera à comprendre les limites des méthodes actuelles, qui ne permettent plus de restituer un état de mer cohérent avec les références disponibles lorsque la vitesse du courant dépasse 1 m/s, comme montré par Lopez et al. (2018). Les méthodes développées seront ensuite évaluées à partir des mesures in situ et des modélisations numériques. Le radar HF constitue ainsi un élément central de ce travail, dont l’amélioration doit permettre de mieux caractériser les états de mer dans les forts courants du Raz Blanchard.

Missions / Activités principales :

Le (la) titulaire du poste sera affecté à l’équipe M3 de l’UMR Lab-STICC et sera en charge des missions principales suivantes :

  • Réaliser une étude bibliographique sur les modèles permettant de décrire l’effet des vagues sur le spectre Doppler mesuré par un radar HF

  • Implémenter un code de simulation intégrant l’effet des vagues à partir d’une description de l’état de mer dans le spectre Doppler

  • Analyser les simulations en les comparant aux mesures réelles pour comprendre l’influence du courant et plus particulièrement des forts courants sur la mesure d’états de mer

  • Proposer et implémenter des évolutions des algorithmes permettant de s’adapter aux forts courants présents sur la zone du Raz Blanchard

Missions / Activité annexe :

 

  • Participer à la démarche Qualité de l’établissement

  • Contribuer à la démarche RSE dans le cadre de ses missions et de ses activités au sein de l’Ecole 

Niveau de diplôme et formations

Les candidats doivent être titulaires d’un doctorat et/ou d’un diplôme d’ingénieur avec expérience dans un domaine pertinent (océanographie physique côtière, traitement du signal, etc…)

 

Emploi

Postes ouverts aux candidats :

  • Agent contractuel

 

Durée d’affectation souhaitée : 18 mois

Date de prise de fonctions prévue : 1er janvier 2027

Rémunération :

  • Contractuels : en fonction de l'expérience professionnelle sur des postes de niveau équivalent

Lieu de travail :

ENSTA Campus de Brest, 2 rue François Verny, 29200 BREST

« Le site est accessible en voiture (parking pour le personnel) ou en transports en commun. L’Ecole étant engagée dans une démarche RSE (DD-RS et employeur pro-vélo), elle encourage aux mobilités douces par la mise en place de dispositif d’aide financière (FMD) et des infrastructures adaptées aux cyclistes ».

Poste à temps complet (25 jours de congés annuels, 23 RTT annuels)

Avantages :

  • Transports (participation forfaitaire de l’employeur à hauteur de 75 %)

  • Forfait mobilité durable (jusqu’à 300€/an)

  • Possibilité de télétravail (après période d’essai et après accord du manager et dépôt d’une demande)

  • Subvention employeur au restaurant administratif et/ou à la cafétéria de l’établissement

  • Comité d’action sociale, avec notamment des événements et animations proposés au personnel, salle de sport sur adhésion,

  • Mutuelle (participation à hauteur de 50% de l’établissement)

Aménagement du poste de travail et recrutement inclusif :

Tous nos postes sont ouverts aux candidats en situation de handicap.

ENSTA s’engage à un recrutement favorisant l’égalité, la diversité et l’inclusion. Toutes les candidatures sans aucune distinction (âge, handicap, sexe, nationalité, religion, orientation sexuelle…) ont leur place dans notre processus de recrutement.

 

Modalités de candidature

  • Une ou plusieurs lettres de recommandation

Présentation de l’Ecole

 

ENSTA est membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris (IP Paris). Dans le cadre d’IP Paris, l’école participe aux activités des centres interdisciplinaires notamment du centre interdisciplinaire d'études pour la Défense et la Sécurité (CIEDS, soutenu par le ministère des armées et l’agence de l’innovation de défense (AID). Elle est à l’origine de la création du Centre interdisciplinaire Mers & Océans, inauguré en janvier 2025. Des chercheurs de l’école travaillent également en collaboration dans le cadre d'études portées par les centres Hi-Paris, lauréat en 2024 IA Cluster, E4C ou E4H notamment.

 

ENSTA résulte de la fusion le 1er janvier 2025 d’ENSTA Paris et d’ENSTA Bretagne. Son siège est situé à Palaiseau (91), sur le campus de Paris-Saclay et elle a un autre campus à Brest. Elle met en place une nouvelle formation d’ingénieur unifiée sur les deux campus (Paris-Saclay et Brest) à la rentrée académique 2026/2027.

 

Rejoindre l'école, c'est intégrer un établissement engagé pour la parité et l'égalité professionnelle, la diversité et l'accompagnement de ses agents en situation de handicap, dès le recrutement et tout au long de la carrière. Afin de préserver le bien-être au travail, l'école mène une politique active en matière de conditions de travail, reposant notamment sur un juste équilibre entre vie personnelle et vie professionnelle.


Connaissances : 

  • Expérience dans la mesure de grandeurs océanographiques :

    - Connaissance en traitement du signal et/ou océanographique physique côtière

  • Expérience en développement informatique :

    - Principalement en Python, des connaissances en C ou Fortran serait un plus

    - Connaissance de Git

Savoir-faire: 

  •   Rédaction de rapports scientifiques et techniques en anglais

  • Préparation et présentation d’exposés scientifiques en anglais

 

Aptitudes: 

  • Autonomie

  • Capacité à travailler en équipe

  • Approche proactive

jobs.description:
AI Engineer Intern (x/f/m) - Nantes

Join a team of passionate and committed people working to improve healthcare.

At Doctolib, our tech teams build products and features that improve the daily lives of healthcare professionals and patients. We work in feature teams within an agile environment, in close collaboration with Product, Design, Data Science, and Business teams.

What you'll do

We are looking for an AI Engineer Intern to join our Tech team and contribute to the development of AI-powered features at Doctolib.

You will work closely with experienced AI and software engineers to explore, prototype, evaluate, and improve AI-based solutions. This internship will give you the opportunity to gain practical experience across the different stages of an AI product, from experimentation to integration into a production environment.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Contribute to the development of AI features and services under the guidance of experienced engineers

  • Write Python code to support prototypes, experiments, evaluation tools, and backend components

  • Experiment with large language models, prompting techniques, retrieval, and tool integration

  • Contribute to automated tests and documentation for the components you develop

  • Investigate issues, analyse results, and suggest improvements to your team

  • Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and team rituals

You will receive regular guidance from your mentor and teammates. The scope of your work will grow progressively as you become familiar with the codebase, the tools, and the technical challenges.

Who you are

Before you read on, if you do not have the exact profile described below but feel that this internship matches your skills and interests, we still encourage you to apply.

You will be a great fit if you:

  • Are in the final year of a degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering, or a related field

  • Have basic experience with Python through coursework, personal projects, research, or previous internships

  • Have a basic understanding of programming concepts, data structures, and software development

  • Are curious about artificial intelligence and interested in understanding how AI systems work

  • Are comfortable communicating in English, both written and spoken

It would be fantastic if you:

  • Have worked on a project involving machine learning, natural language processing, or large language models

  • Have used agentic frameworks like Langchain or Google ADK.

  • Have experimented with AI APIs, prompting, retrieval, or conversational interfaces

  • Have experience in taking products to production and supporting them with real users.

  • Have some experience with Git, APIs, testing, or data analysis

  • Have an interest in healthcare, privacy, or responsible AI

Life at Doctolib Tech

Our products are built on a cloud-native platform that supports web and mobile applications across several countries and healthcare systems.

Even if Doctolib uses technologies like Ruby on Rails, TypeScript, Java, Kotlin, Swift, React Native, and many cloud-related technologies, the principal language you'll work on is Python.You will also have the opportunity to use AI-assisted development tools within our engineering practices.

Discover our AI vision here and learn more about our tech culture on the Doctolib Tech site.

What we offer

  • A structured internship with dedicated mentoring

  • The opportunity to work on real AI projects in a healthcare environment

  • Technical learning sessions and access to internal engineering communities

  • Access to AI tools for coding, development, and learning

  • Meal vouchers

  • Free breakfast in the office

  • Up to 2 days of remote work per week

  • A flexible workplace policy, depending on the team and location

  • A collaborative and international working environment

The interview process

  • Coding Game

  • Recruiter Interview

  • Technical Interview

  • Behavioral Interview

Job details

  • Internship, 6 months, full-time

  • Location: Nantes

  • Hybrid work setup, up to 2 remote days per week

  • Start date: March 2027

We welcome everyone

At Doctolib, we are committed to improving access to healthcare for everyone. We evaluate candidates based on their qualifications, motivation, and potential, without discrimination.

The more diverse ideas are heard, the better our products can serve patients and healthcare professionals. We welcome applications regardless of gender, religion, age, sexual orientation, ethnicity, disability, or place of origin.

To support an inclusive recruitment process, we invite you to leave personal information such as pictures and age off your application. If you require an accommodation during the interview process, please let us know.

Join us in building the healthcare we all dream of!

Horizon3 is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find and fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZeroTM platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by ITOps/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs.

We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools, false positives resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

jobs.title: AI Product Manager
jobs.description:
AI Product Manager

Le Product Management, c'est notre ADN. L'IA, c'est ce qui est en train de changer le métier.

Chez Hubvisory, tu ne te contentes pas de gérer un backlog : tu deviens la référence produit incontournable pour accompagner nos clients grands comptes dans la transformation de leurs produits digitaux et de leurs organisations. Ce poste ajoute une dimension : tu pilotes des produits dans lesquels l'IA devient une brique fonctionnelle à part entière, et tu t'en sers aussi pour accélérer ta propre pratique de PM.

Ce que tu fais concrètement :

  • Tu conduis les phases de Discovery de bout en bout. Entretiens utilisateurs, cadrage des besoins, personas et benchmarks : tu identifies les problèmes réels pour construire les solutions qui comptent. Et tu sais reconnaître, parmi ces problèmes, ceux que l'IA résout vraiment de ceux qu'elle complique.

  • Tu qualifies les cas d'usage IA avant de les construire. Faisabilité, valeur, coût, données disponibles, risque d'erreur acceptable : tu instruis le sujet avec rigueur. Tu portes la décision de ne pas faire d'IA quand elle ne se justifie pas : c'est aussi ça, la maturité sur le sujet.

  • Tu embarques l'IA dans le produit, pas à côté. Tu travailles main dans la main avec les data scientists et les AI engineers : définition de ce qu'est un « bon » résultat, seuils de confiance, stratégies de repli quand le modèle se trompe, interfaces qui rendent l'incertitude lisible pour l'utilisateur, boucles de retour pour progresser dans le temps.

  • Tu pilotes des périmètres produit complexes et interdépendants. Règles métier, états et transitions, cohérence entre plusieurs surfaces (interface interne et parcours client en ligne), contrats d'intégration avec les produits adjacents : tu tiens la vue d'ensemble et tu stabilises ce qui doit l'être, dans des écosystèmes où ton produit n'est jamais seul.

  • Tu prends la donnée en main. Tu interprètes toi-même les insights, tu structures des hypothèses, tu mesures pour décider, pas pour afficher. Une vraie maturité data, c'est ce qui distingue les PM junior des PM qui créent de la valeur, et c'est le socle sans lequel aucun produit IA ne tient.

  • Tu mesures l'impact. Tu définis et analyses les KPI et OKR pour t'assurer que le produit sert les objectifs business, tout en animant les rituels agiles pour maintenir une dynamique d'équipe exemplaire.

  • Tu participes à la vie d'Hubvisory. Tu consolides ta posture de consultant, tu partages tes retours d'expérience et tu évolues, selon tes aspirations, vers des rôles de Product Leader ou Manager Conseil.

Bonus : tu as déjà outillé ton propre quotidien de PM avec l'IA : rédaction et structuration de specs, dépouillement d'entretiens utilisateurs, exploration de données, prototypage rapide ? On aime les PM qui testent, qui gardent ce qui marche et qui savent dire ce qui ne marche pas.


👉 Pourquoi rejoindre Hubvisory ?

  • Hubvisory est le seul cabinet en France focalisé exclusivement sur le Product Management et l'IA. Pas de practice data généraliste, pas de conseil en transformation sur tous les sujets. On fait une chose, on la fait bien, on la fait avec les meilleurs clients.

  • Un parcours d'accompagnement sur-mesure. Si tu es PO aujourd'hui et que tu veux devenir PM, on te donne les moyens : mentorship, cas complexes, retours structurés. Nos rituels collectifs (Hub'Times) et nos revalorisations bi-annuelles récompensent la vraie progression, pas l'ancienneté.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Cloud Partner Integrations
jobs.description:
Senior Software Engineer - Cloud Partner Integrations

About the team

Most providers make customers migrate their data to them. We're doing the opposite: bringing ClickHouse Cloud into the environments our customers already trust, so their data stays useful right where it lives.

Those environments come in a few shapes. Some are major cloud data platforms that run ClickHouse as a native service, so customers get it without leaving the tool they already use. Some are BI and visualization tools that need ClickHouse to show up as a fast, first-class data source behind their dashboards. And some are developer and data platforms we connect through marketplaces and identity federation with a couple of clicks or agentic calls. Every integration is unique, but the goal is the same every time: ClickHouse should feel like a first-class citizen in every environment.

The craft is finding the patterns underneath different integrations. As one of the first backend engineers, you'll help shape the technical defaults for this team. You'll have end-to-end ownership, but you'll also work inside the constraints of platforms you don't own: thin documentation, unfamiliar deployment topologies, and timelines governed by partner approval cycles. A lot of the challenge is engineering across trust boundaries you don't fully control.

You won't be doing it alone. You'll work closely with your engineering manager, the product manager, a growing team, and experienced engineers across the broader org. If that sounds like your kind of challenge, let's talk.

What you'll do

You'll own an integration end to end: the design, the code, and the production system that keeps running after launch. The patterns you set there become defaults the rest of the team builds on.

Day to day, that looks like:

  • Owning the architecture: auth and identity flows, multi-tenancy, how data moves and where it's allowed to live, performance, and what happens in production

  • Running what you build. Which means owning the infrastructure, CI, deployment, observability behind it and on-call

  • Working on top of external platforms you can't change, and being straight about which risks are yours to manage and which aren't

  • Partnering closely with the internal teams whose services you depend on: iterating on product requirements, agreeing on interfaces and protocols, and proactively finding ways to keep moving

About you

These are the attributes of someone who will perform well in this role:

  • 8+ years building software, with a good chunk of it on data-heavy or integration-flavored systems

  • Preferably proficient in TypeScript or Go or comfortable contributing to each

  • Solid backend and systems instincts. You can reason about deployment topology, multi-tenancy, and data movement, and you're comfortable owning architectural tradeoffs you'll have to live with later

  • You've worked with modern auth protocols, service principals, and identity federation, and you know how to get it right across a trust boundary

  • You've built on someone else's platform and know what that's actually like: incomplete docs, unintended breaking changes, etc.

  • You're comfortable in ambiguity. You can ship before the spec is finished, make sensible calls under uncertainty, and flag the decisions that'll be hard to undo to your team before we bake them in.

  • You're good with other engineers. Much of the work runs through teams you don't own, and you earn their trust by how you think, not just what you commit.

  • You're mainly a backend engineer, but you're comfortable enough to touch a modern React app

  • You use AI tools well and honestly. Reach for Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or whatever helps, and be clear about where you did and didn't

  • You write well. Most of how we coordinate happens async in chats, design docs and RFCs

Nice to have

None of these are required, but any of them would be a bonus:

  • Close familiarity with a major cloud data or analytics platform ecosystem

  • Real depth in auth and identity federation, or experience building to a partner's security review, marketplace requirements or certification requirements

  • Hands-on experience designing multi-tenant SaaS platforms, or the isolation and deployment topology behind them

  • Working knowledge of ClickHouse, or another columnar / OLAP engine

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

  • Equity in the company - Every new eligible team member who joins our company receives equity.

  • Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

  • A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

  • Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

Equal Opportunity & Privacy

ClickHouse provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type based on factors such as race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

Please see here for our Privacy Statement.

Senior Treasury Specialist

Build with us

Since 2004, we've had one clear goal: to make payments and money management effortless for every business in Europe.

Today, more than 250,000 companies use Mollie to get paid, manage money and grow – with products designed to be simple, scalable, and dependable. We're building for the long term, so we provide the tools you need, processes you can rely on, and a balanced work environment to help you do work you're proud of.

Sound like your kind of place? Let's build together.

Your impact

As a Treasury Specialist at Mollie, you play a critical role in managing our cash, banks, foreign currency positions and investments. You also actively support the design and roll out of our Financial Services products.

You're not just part of the CFO team. You're an integral part of the Financial Services Domain, and you're responsible for driving product improvements across multiple problem spaces, from Cash Management and Reporting to Banking Interactions. You bring a strong understanding of cash management, FX and investments, plus great drive and strong analytical skills.

 

This role suits you if you're not afraid of hands-on work and you also want to work on new strategic initiatives and product development in a fast-paced environment. You'll join our Merchant Finance and Treasury Team in Amsterdam.

What you'll ship

  • Cash management activities that run smoothly, alongside better reporting and forecasting processes.

  • Mollie's excess cash and multi-million investment portfolio, managed to get the most out of our money.

  • Policies and procedures on Treasury and Financial Risk topics, developed and kept up to date.

  • Uncovered FX risk positions identified, with clear recommendations on how to manage them.

  • A banking infrastructure built and optimised for efficient, cost-effective payments.

  • Company-wide growth projects and projects across domains, including new products and payment methods, that help Mollie build first class finance and treasury products for our customers.

  • A treasury management system developed further, to support more automation of our Treasury operations.

What you'll bring

  • At least 5 years of relevant Treasury experience, with knowledge of international cash management, forecasting, foreign exchange management and internal controls.

  • An advanced degree, preferably in Finance or Business Administration, a comparable study, or demonstrably a comparable level of knowledge and thinking.

  • You like to get things done and bring energy to solve problems for our customers and internal stakeholders. You're proactive, analytical and take strong ownership.

  • A mindset that looks for solutions, and the ability to come up with new ideas to improve our products and services.

  • You're a confident communicator with excellent spoken and written English. You can align and influence stakeholders across Finance, Product and the wider business, and explain complex treasury topics clearly to non-specialists.

  • You enjoy sharing knowledge and supporting less experienced colleagues, and you're comfortable contributing to domain-wide knowledge sharing.

Grow your way

At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.

You'll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way. Many Mollies move into new roles or take on new projects to stretch themselves, and we actively hire from within to help you take the next step.

No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.

jobs.description:
Senior Staff Engineer - Stablecoin

About Payoneer

Founded in 2005, Payoneer is the global financial platform that removes friction from doing business across borders, with a mission to connect the world’s underserved businesses to a rising global economy. We’re a community with over 2,500 colleagues all over the world, working to serve customers, and partners in over 190 countries and territories.

By taking the complexity out of the financial workflows–including everything from global payments and compliance to multi-currency and workforce management, to providing working capital and business intelligence–we give businesses the tools they need to work efficiently worldwide and grow with confidence.

Role summary

PAYO Digital Bank, N.A. (PDB), Payoneer's national trust bank subsidiary, is seeking a deeply experienced Senior Staff Engineer to serve as the technical anchor of the bank's engineering organization and the architect of record for its core transactional systems. You will own the design of the integration between the core banking ledger and the stablecoin issuance engine: the system of record that reconciles fiat reserves, on-chain token supply, and customer balances with bank-grade accuracy and auditability.

This is a high-impact, hands-on architecture and leadership role reporting directly to the Chief Technology Officer of PDB, providing technical direction to the core team of engineers.

The ideal candidate is a distributed systems expert with high-integrity transactional experience (banking core, payments ledger, exchange, or settlement infrastructure). You must be able to defend architectural decisions to independent auditors and OCC examiners, and build engineering culture as deliberately as you build systems.

Candidates must be based in New York, NY OR Miami, FL | Full-time

What you'll do

  • Core Architecture Ownership: Architect and build the bank's core backend, including microservices, transactional persistence schemas, event messaging endpoints, and internal APIs, documented to a standard suitable for OCC examination.
  • Ledger & Stablecoin Integration: Design the reconciliation architecture guaranteeing absolute consistency between the fiat subledger, reserve accounts, and on-chain token supply. Build the event messaging layer securely synchronizing core ledger transactions with custody platform mint/burn actions.
  • Technical Leadership: Serve as the technical lead and mentor for the Core Backend team. Establish uncompromising standards for code reviews, testing, observability, and deployment appropriate for a regulated bank.
  • Compliance in the Transaction Path: Integrate automated sanctions screening connectors with auditable screening and case escalation hooks.
  • Resilience & Observability: Partner with the SRE Lead on multi-region availability, failover targets, and real-time ledger alerting. Work with the Security division on IAM, key management interfaces, and threat modeling for mint/burn pipelines.
  • Audit Readiness: Support UAT, feature freezes, and external control validation ahead of the pre-opening exam.

Who you are

  • Engineering Depth: 12+ years of software engineering experience, including 5+ years hands-on architecting high-integrity transactional systems (banking core, payments ledger, exchange, or settlement infrastructure).
  • Distributed Systems Expertise: Deep understanding of event-driven architecture, exactly-once processing semantics, idempotency, and reconciliation at scale.
  • Cloud-Native Infrastructure: Hands-on experience with Kubernetes, Infrastructure-as-Code, and multi-region deployment in a regulated or audited environment.
  • Audit-Grade Engineering: Track record designing immutable transaction logs, reconciliation controls, and automated evidence generation for examiners and external auditors.
  • Technical Mentorship: Proven success elevating the technical output of senior engineers, setting architectural standards, and owning delivery end-to-end.
  • Regulator-Ready Documentation: Ability to produce system architecture documentation that withstands intense regulatory and audit scrutiny.

Not a must but a great advantage:

  • Digital Asset Systems: Direct experience with stablecoin, digital asset custody, or blockchain settlement systems, including on-chain/off-chain reconciliation.
  • Examination Environments: Familiarity with FFIEC IT examination expectations or SOC 2 audit environments.

Why This Role Matters Every dollar of PAYO-USD in circulation depends on the systems this role designs. The Senior Staff Engineer builds the transactional backbone that regulators examine, auditors verify, and merchants trust.

Principal/Staff Product Manager, Risk Advisory

About Us

Fieldguide is establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets through automating and streamlining the work of advisory, audit, and tax practitioners at the world's largest CPA firms. Put simply, we build software for the people who enable trust between businesses.

We're based in San Francisco, CA, but built as a remote-first company that enables you to do your best work from anywhere. We're backed by top investors including Goldman Sachs, Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, and Y Combinator.

We value diversity, in backgrounds and in experiences. We need people from all backgrounds and walks of life to help build the future of audit and advisory. Fieldguide's team is inclusive, driven, humble, and supportive. We are deliberate and self-reflective about the kind of team and culture we are building, seeking teammates who are not only strong in their own aptitudes but care deeply about supporting each other's growth.

As a growth stage startup employee, you'll have the opportunity to build the future of business trust. We make audit practitioners' lives easier by eliminating up to 50% of their work and giving them better work-life balance. If you share our values and enthusiasm for building a great culture and product, you will find a home at Fieldguide.

About the Role

Fieldguide is the market leader in AI-native software for risk advisory and assurance practitioners, working with the majority of the top 100 accounting firms. Our agents already support work across risk advisory frameworks, including SOC, PCI and HITRUST. Now we’re taking the next step: agents that carry the whole advisory engagement, from scoping through sign-off, with practitioners stepping in only for exceptions and judgment calls.

As Principal/Staff Product Manager for Advisory, you will help shape the product strategy and roadmap that extends our agents from individual workflows to the full engagement lifecycle. You'll be building from a position of strength, with customers who already trust us and who are skeptical, expert and deeply invested in the quality of their work.

What You'll Do

  • Shape the strategy for the end-to-end agentic advisory engagement, and own the roadmap and execution that connect planning, testing and review into a single experience managed by agents

  • Define how practitioners supervise agents: what stays human, how exceptions surface, and how corrections make the agents better over time

  • Work with engineering, design and our AI quality teams to extend our agents across frameworks and engagement phases, with measurable evals and ground truth you help define

  • Work directly with partners, methodology owners and practitioners at top firms, including onsite, and bring what you learn back into the roadmap

  • Partner with customer success, sales and marketing to communicate the strategy and drive adoption of agentic workflows across our largest accounts

Who You Are

  • 10+ years of product management experience, including leading a major product line at the staff level or equivalent

  • Experience shipping AI agents in production for a B2B product, with evals and a clear approach to quality, not just AI features

  • Strong familiarity with advisory and assurance work (SOC 2, PCI, HITRUST, ISO or NIST), either as a practitioner or as a PM who built software for it.

  • Strong technical fluency: comfortable talking with engineers about LLM and agent architecture, evals, and trade-offs without needing to write code

  • Able to hold a strategic position under sustained pressure from commercial stakeholders and our largest customers, and to change it when the argument is genuinely good

  • Comfortable working with detail-oriented, skeptical audiences and translating their workflow into product requirements.

More About Fieldguide

Fieldguide is a values-based company. Our values are:

  • Fearless: Inspire and break down seemingly impossible walls.

  • Fast: Launch fast with excellence, iterate to perfection.

  • Lovable: Deliver happiness and 11 star experiences.

  • Owners: Execute and run the business with ownership.

  • Win-win: Create mutual value and earn trust for life.

  • Competitive compensation packages with meaningful ownership

  • Flexible PTO

  • 401k

  • Wellness benefits, including a bundle of free therapy sessions

  • Technology and Work from Home reimbursement

You will be the Director/Senior Director of Fieldguide's internal audit product: own the P&L, set the strategy, and take it from first design partners to a repeatable, multi-million-dollar business.

Internal audit teams carry the same capacity problem as external auditors, often with smaller budgets: rising SOX and regulatory scope, new risk areas like AI, cyber and third parties, and a shrinking talent pool. This role takes that engine to a new buyer: Chief Audit Executives and internal audit leaders at corporations, plus the firms that deliver co-sourced and outsourced internal audit for them.

This is not a product management or a sales role. You will make the calls a founder makes: which internal audit workflows to attack first, which companies are the first customers, what to build next and what to kill. You will have a dedicated pod of engineers, designers and internal audit subject-matter experts, and the full weight of Fieldguide's platform, brand and firm relationships behind you.

  • Find the wedge. Spend real time inside internal audit functions with CAEs, audit directors, SOX program leads and staff auditors. Identify the high-volume, high-pain work (SOX controls testing, walkthroughs, evidence collection, risk assessments, operational audits) where an agent can do the job end to end, and decide which problem we win first.

  • Build the product with the pod. Partner with engineering, and design leads and our internal audit SMEs to define what ships, in what order, and what "good enough" means for work that lands in front of audit committees and external auditors. Write the spec when needed; sit in the eval reviews.

  • Land design partners, then customers. Help close the first 5–10 internal audit teams. Turn them into referenceable deployments with measurable hours saved, coverage gained and quality improved.

  • Partner with GTM. Work with Sales, Marketing and Customer Success to shape how the product is positioned, sold and expanded: into corporate IA teams directly and through co-sourcing firms already on Fieldguide. Bring the customer insight and proof points they need, and help build a playbook they can run without you.

  • Know the landscape. Understand where incumbent GRC and audit-management tools stop, and position Fieldguide as the system that does the work, not just tracks it.

  • Build the team. Hire the first dedicated GTM, deployment and IA SME roles for the line as it scales.

  • Know when to double down or stop. Run tight experiments, read the signal honestly, and bring the company a clear recommendation.

  • Real P&L or revenue ownership, with numbers you can talk through.

jobs.title: Legal Counsel
jobs.description:
Legal Counsel

About Us_
// At Masabi, we’re driving the fare payment revolution, powering the journeys of millions all over the world. We build fare collection platforms that allow riders to seamlessly buy and present tickets for public transport either on their mobile phones, from a ticket machine, or even by tapping their bank card to travel.

Our Justride platform is used in over 250 locations globally, including some of the largest cities in the world. With our industry-first mobile ticketing SDK, we’ve partnered with large players in the transport space, including Uber, Moovit and Transit.

Your own journey is important to us too. Choosing a role here means joining a network of innovators from all walks of life; a group of passionate individuals who consistently deliver. Here, you’ll find the tools you need to build the career you want. Whether you’re taking the direct route or trying a new path, we’ll support you no matter what.

The Role_

// At Masabi, we're building technology that makes public transport simpler, fairer and more accessible for millions of people. Behind every agency that runs on our platform is a commercial agreement someone had to shape, negotiate and close.

As our Legal Counsel, you'll work closely with our General Counsel, leading on our largest and most complex commercial deals.

Much of the work follows one opportunity from beginning to end. It starts with major tenders and public procurements, where you'll shape our position on the terms we can work with and the ones worth challenging. From there you'll take the deal through negotiation to signature, with colleagues across the business bringing the commercial and technical detail. Underneath runs the advisory side: data protection and privacy, IP and licensing, and the questions that come with operating across several markets.

You'll work directly with our CEO, CFO and CPO, helping them see risk clearly and decide quickly. Legal is a close-knit team, so you'll have genuine influence over how we work. Our biggest markets are the UK and North America, though we work well beyond both, so the jurisdictions and deal types will vary.

Location_

// This role is available on a remote basis for candidates located anywhere in the UK. Candidates based in London may also work in a hybrid model, with occasional travel to the office.

Responsibilities_

  • Take the lead on the legal side of major tenders and public procurements, shaping our position on the terms and where we're willing to move

  • Lead the negotiation and close of our largest customer contracts, working with colleagues across the business to settle the commercial, technical and operational detail alongside the legal

  • Carry major opportunities from first look through to a signed contract

  • Draft and negotiate across our full commercial range, including SaaS and licensing, implementation and professional services, NDAs, data processing terms, and partnership and reseller agreements

  • Advise the business on data protection and privacy, IP and licensing, and the commercial questions that come up day to day

  • Work directly with our CEO, CFO and CPO, translating legal risk into commercial choices they can act on

  • Use our AI and agentic tooling as part of how you work, and help shape where Legal takes it next

  • Step in for our General Counsel during periods of leave, or when he's committed elsewhere

About You_

  • You hold a law degree and a current practising certificate, qualified in the UK, the US, or a Commonwealth jurisdiction such as Australia, New Zealand, Ireland or Canada

  • Several years in practice since qualifying

  • You have strong, hands-on experience drafting and negotiating complex technology contracts, particularly SaaS, and have led those negotiations yourself

  • Communicates with precision, giving you a clear answer to a senior stakeholder without unnecessary detail

  • You're comfortable across a broad remit, moving between a major negotiation and a smaller advisory question in the same day

  • Has worked across more than one jurisdiction

  • You think ahead as well as answering what's in front of you, when the same issue keeps coming back, you'd rather change how it's handled than answer it a third time

  • Builds trust easily across a business, so people tend to bring you in early rather than once a decision is already made

  • You're interested in how AI can support legal work, with a clear sense of where judgement stays with you

  • Trusts your own judgement on risk, and you're comfortable standing by it

  • You can have the harder conversations with senior people and come out of them on good terms

We don't expect you to tick every box. What matters most is curiosity, a willingness to learn, and the motivation to take ownership of your work.

Nice To Have_

  • Public sector procurement experience, particularly in North America

  • Experience in public transport, mobility, fare collection, payments or another regulated infrastructure environment

  • Several years in private practice before moving in-house

AI at Masabi_

// AI is becoming part of how we work at Masabi. You don’t need professional experience using AI tools, but we’d expect you’ve experimented with them and are curious about how they can help you learn, solve problems, and work more effectively.

Some of Our Benefits_

  • 25 days of holiday per year plus the option to buy another 5 days, pro-rated

  • Private healthcare via AXA, including pre-existing conditions and mental health

  • Life insurance

  • Menopause support

  • Choice of workstation

  • The ability to work for up to 3 months per year from any country in the world (certain limitations apply)

  • Pension scheme

  • Training allowance of up to £1000 per year

  • £200 annual allowance for any home office need or improvement

  • Enhanced family leave pay

  • Cycle to work scheme

  • Regular social gatherings with a monthly allowance for each employee

  • A fun and collaborative environment with a focus on making a difference in the world

Careers at Masabi are for people going places - driven by a mission to make transit fair and accessible for all.

// We are a network of innovators from all walks of life, passionate about making a difference. At Masabi, we operate with openness and trust, creating an environment where everyone feels empowered to bring their whole, authentic selves to work.

Whoever you are, just be yourself.
// We welcome applications from underrepresented groups, including disabled and neurodivergent people, and can make adjustments at any stage of the process. You’re also welcome to share your pronouns whenever you feel comfortable. Together, we simplify journeys, remove barriers, and improve daily life for millions.

Why Join Masabi?

  • Driven by Purpose – We believe in journeys made simple. The work isn’t always easy, but the best things never are.

  • Encouraged to Accelerate – Masabi is going places and our people are in the driving seat. Whether you’re taking the direct route or exploring new paths, we support your journey.

  • Advancing with Empathy – We put people first and foster a culture of learning, not blame. No matter your cargo, we share the load.

We’re already powering journeys - are you ready to join us?

Who we are

Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables.

We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi. The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level.

We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann, and Sauraj Gambhir, and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun.

In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years.

About the Role

We spend tens of millions per year on GPU compute to train tabular foundation models. That's not a target, it's what we're running today, and it's growing. The person who owns this infrastructure makes decisions worth millions of dollars: cluster architecture, scheduling efficiency, provider strategy, hardware selection.

Today we run on Slurm across multiple clusters. We're scaling to multi-cluster, multi-provider infrastructure using SkyPilot and evaluating new hardware generations as they come online. You own the full stack, from cluster orchestration and cost optimization to CI/CD, automation, and the tooling that keeps researchers moving fast. You work directly with the research team and understand what they're doing well enough to make infrastructure decisions that actually help them.

What you'll work on:

  • Own and evolve multi-cluster GPU infrastructure, from Slurm and SkyPilot on GCP today to multi-provider orchestration and new GPU generations tomorrow. Drive architecture, automated provisioning, workload scheduling, reliability, cost optimization, and capacity planning against growing compute demands

  • Build the developer productivity layer: CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, reproducible environments, experiment tracking, and internal tooling that keeps research iteration speed high

  • Improve infrastructure reliability through monitoring, observability, infrastructure as code, and automation. Reduce operational toil and make complex systems easier to manage.

  • Help guide compute spending decisions. You understand cost per FLOP across providers and hardware, and you hate wasted compute

Tech stack: Slurm, SkyPilot, GCP (+ AWS and Azure to come), Docker, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Python, uv, wandb

You may be a good fit if you have:

  • 3+ years building and operating production infrastructure at scale, ideally involving compute clusters, distributed training systems, or HPC

  • Hands-on experience with cluster management and workload orchestration systems such as Slurm, Kubernetes, or similar technologies. You've debugged scheduling failures and operated infrastructure where downtime has real cost

  • Experience designing and maintaining CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and reliable build and deployment workflows

  • Strong systems engineering fundamentals: Linux, networking, storage, and distributed systems. You're comfortable debugging complex infrastructure problems across the stack.

  • Strong Python skills and enough familiarity with training to profile a run and tell whether the bottleneck is data loading, communication, or compute

  • Track record of making infrastructure decisions that measurably improved reliability, developer productivity, or cost efficiency

  • Strong AI tooling skills. You use Claude Code, Cursor, or similar fluently to move fast without sacrificing quality

Bonus:

  • Familiarity with GPU infrastructure, PyTorch, GPU profiling, and distributed training

  • Experience operating at tens-of-millions-scale compute spend

  • Multi-cloud or hybrid HPC/cloud infrastructure experience

  • Experience scaling from single cluster to multi-cluster orchestration

  • Background building experiment tracking, model registries, or ML pipeline tooling

Life at Prior Labs

You'll work alongside researchers and builders who hold themselves to a very high bar - in the quality of their work and in how they work with each other. We move fast and still take the time to do things right.

Our teams are based in Berlin, Freiburg, and New York - when you're working on something as hard as TabPFN, being in the same room matters. But great people come from everywhere, and in exceptional cases we're open to remote, which usually means frequent travel to one of our offices. Wherever you're based, the whole company comes together regularly for offsites to build and celebrate together.

Our Commitments

The best products and teams are built by people with a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds. We welcome applications from all identities and walks of life - especially if you've ever felt discouraged by "not checking every box" - and provide equal opportunities regardless of gender, sexual orientation, origin, disability, or any other trait that makes you who you are.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager
jobs.description:
Senior Program Manager

About us

INCO is a leading social enterprise on a mission to shape a more inclusive and sustainable economy that creates opportunities for all. We have teams and programs in over 50 countries. Our work spans five complementary activities:

  1. INCO Academy: skilling programs for people facing barriers to employment, leading to careers in fast-growing industries such as technology, sustainability and healthcare (400,000+ job seekers trained to date).

  2. INCO Kids: education and awareness programs giving school-age learners future-proof knowledge in technology, sustainability, citizenship and more (350,000+ learners supported to date).

  3. INCO Entrepreneurs: incubation and acceleration for underrepresented founders and social entrepreneurs (2,000+ businesses supported every year).

  4. INCO Ventures: impact investing and funding for social and environmental impact startups (€500M+ assets under management).

  5. INCO Spaces: co-working and co-living spaces for social and environmental innovators (Paris, Berlin, Warsaw and more).

About the program:

AI and the Future of Work is a new three-year research and policy-engagement program (2026–2029), funded through a research grant partnership and led end to end by INCO. It tracks AI's real-world impact on jobs, tasks and productivity across all 27 EU member states, and gives policymakers the evidence, trend baselines and scenario-planning tools to capture AI's productivity upside while managing the workforce transition.

About the role:

We are looking for a Senior Program Manager to run the AI and the Future of Work program day to day and make sure it delivers on time, on budget and to the grant's commitments. You will closely lead and collaborate with a Research Lead and a Policy Lead. 

You will turn a three-year grant into a working operation: a deliverables calendar across 27 countries, a consortium of up to 15 partners, a publication schedule and a reporting cycle the funder can trust. You need to be comfortable working alongside researchers and policy specialists, and fluent in the rhythm of grant-funded research programs.

Responsibilities:

Lead program delivery end to end 

Planning and implementation

  • Build and own the three-year implementation plan: workstreams, milestones, dependencies and the deliverables calendar agreed with the funder.

  • Run the program's operating rhythm: weekly core-team check-ins, monthly consortium updates and quarterly steering reviews.

  • Coordinate the publication pipeline with the Research and Policy Leads: quarterly data refreshes, five semi-annual reports, policy briefs, the annual flagship and the 2029 EU27 report.

  • Keep thorough program documentation: plans, decision logs, risk register and handover notes.

  • Set up quality-assurance steps for outputs (review cycles, sign-off, editorial and brand checks) together with the Communications team.

  • Run the semi-annual tracking cycle and the reporting calendar for the five P0 markets and five sub-regional clusters, so national and EU27 outputs land together.

Monitoring and evaluation

  • Define and track program KPIs and grant deliverables; spot slippage early and agree corrective action with the leads.

  • Collect and compile performance data across workstreams and partners, and report it to your manager and the funder in a structured, actionable way.

  • Coordinate the program's evaluation framework so the team can show what the evidence changed in policy and practice.

Budget and resources

  • Own the program budget and cost sheet, including consortium partner budgets and the research consolidation budget held by the Research Lead.

  • Manage timelines and scope so the program delivers within the grant's budget and rules; prepare budget forecasts and reallocation requests.

  • Ensure grant compliance: eligible costs, audit trail, data protection (GDPR) and the funder's reporting requirements, working with Finance and Legal.

Manage the consortium and partners 

  • Run the operational side of partner onboarding with the Research Lead: due diligence, contracts, scopes of work, payment schedules and data-sharing agreements.

  • Track the delivery of 8 to 15 national partners against their contracts, and manage underperformance or replacement when needed.

  • Organise consortium working groups, review cycles and annual convenings, and keep communication flowing across countries and time zones.

  • Run the secretariat for the sub-recipient advisory committee (INCO staff, funder representatives and independent experts): schedule meetings, prepare selection materials, record recommendations and keep the process transparent, with final selection resting with INCO.

  • Manage subrecipient compliance: flow-down of grant terms, financial and narrative reporting from partners, and checks before each payment.

Manage the funder and stakeholders

  • Act as the primary operational liaison with the grant funder, keeping expectations aligned and surfacing risks early.

  • Prepare and present progress, financial and impact reports to the funder and other key stakeholders.

  • Work with the Head of Partnerships on funder conversations, renewals and any extension of the partnership.

  • Support the Policy Lead and with the logistics of policymaker convenings, events and launches.

  • Coordinate, with the Policy Lead, the expanded public-engagement activity in Poland and the CEE region, and the logistics of rapid, fact-based responses when AI labour market stories break.

Coordinate the team

  • Set clear responsibilities, timelines and objectives across the core team, and track progress against them.

  • Act as the connecting point between the Research Lead, the Policy Lead, data engineers and INCO's support teams (Communications, Finance, Legal, HR).

  • Identify staffing needs as the program grows (for example research assistants, data roles or a program officer), write job descriptions, interview and onboard new team members, and manage any program staff assigned to you.

Support growth 

  • Work with leadership to standardise how INCO runs grant-funded research programs, so lessons from this one carry over.

  • Identify follow-on funding and adjacent opportunities, for example linking findings to INCO Academy skilling programs.

  • Build relationships across the European research and policy ecosystem.



Essential

  • At least five years managing complex, multi-partner programs, ideally grant-funded research, policy or public-interest programs in Europe.

  • Proven track record managing funders or institutional partners, including donor reporting, budgets and grant compliance.

  • Experience coordinating consortia or networks of external partners, including contracts, scopes of work and partner payments.

  • At least four years leading teams and working cross-functionally, including with senior experts you do not line manage.

  • Strong budget and financial management skills, with ownership of program cost sheets and forecasts.

  • High digital collaboration literacy (Slack, Monday.com, Notion, G-Suite or similar) and comfort running remote work across many countries.

  • Professional English, written and spoken.

  • Strong attention to detail and organisational skills, with excellent communication, versatility and integrity.

Desirable

  • Experience with EU-funded or foundation-funded research programs (for example Horizon Europe, Erasmus+ or major philanthropic grants).

  • Familiarity with research operations: publication cycles, data protection (GDPR), research ethics and data-sharing agreements.

  • Interest in AI, the labour market, skills or the future of work; familiarity with EU institutions such as Cedefop, Eurostat, Eurofound or the JRC.

  • A second EU language, especially German, French, Spanish, Italian or Polish.

  • A recognised project management certification (for example PMP or PRINCE2).

  • Experience managing sub-grants or sub-recipients, including selection processes and flow-down compliance.

jobs.title: Enterprise Deployment Strategist
jobs.description:
Enterprise Deployment Strategist

about us

Every 10 minutes, 18 million conversations happen between businesses and consumers around the world.

For decades, the consumer side of those conversations sucked: long queues, robotic menus, repeated explanations, and advice that is often unhelpful. Most people today still cannot simply say what their problem is in natural language when communicating with businesses.

AI changes that. For the first time, companies can have natural conversations with customers at massive scale. Every B2C company - from energy providers to telcos to insurers - will use AI agents to talk to their customers. The number of conversations businesses will handle is going to explode in the coming years.

At telli, we are solving the challenges that come with that shift. Today, leading B2C companies like Sky are already using telli to deploy thousands of voice agents to provide their customers with a new experience. But building a first voice agent is easy, getting it to drive real outcomes for customers and businesses is the hard part. telli helps companies build, deploy, and improve consumer-facing AI voice agents at scale. This will become one of the most important software categories of the next decade, and we intend to win it.

Full Stack Developer

We Are Sparta

Sparta is the AI leader for commodity trading, home to Leonidas AI, the first operating system for oil and commodity traders.

Backed by $42 million in Series B funding led by One Peak, with participation from returning investors FirstMark and Singular, the same investors behind AI leaders like Legora, Dataiku, and Synthesia. Most companies are building a chatbot on top of data. We've built an agent with an actual reasoning layer, grounded in years of proprietary market data and in-house trading expertise nobody else has.

We're scaling fast, and it's an exciting time to join. From independents to multinationals, the world's leading commodity teams use Sparta and Leonidas AI to move faster, trade smarter, and stay ahead of the market.

At Sparta, you'll be trusted to take ownership, backed by a team who wants you to succeed. AI is how we build here, not just what we sell. Good ideas move fast, and yours could go from staging to production in a couple of hours, whatever department you're in. You'll be challenged, supported, and given room to grow, building the AI that's changing how commodity trading gets done.

Your work has reach. From shaping Leonidas AI, to powering smarter decisions for traders around the world, to changing how commodity trading is done. And because we're growing fast, you'll accelerate your career with a level of ownership and impact you simply won't get at bigger, slower-moving companies.

The role

You build the experience traders see when they work with Leonidas AI: a streaming, branching conversation where agents answer with live price tiles, charts, ARB analysis and sources, inside our app and wherever traders already work, such as Microsoft Teams and Excel. You own features end to end, from the backend-for-frontend to the component in a trader's hands.

This is a full stack role for the agentic era. The interface is no longer a set of fixed screens: it renders what an agent decides to show, as it thinks. You make that feel instant, trustworthy and easy to act on.

What you will do

  • Build agentic UI. Streaming chat, typed blocks parsed mid-stream, tool-call status, branching threads, and dashboards that turn an answer into something a trader can watch.

  • Own the BFF. Route handlers, auth, persistence of conversations and blocks, and the contract between the front end and the agent runtime.

  • Surface data people trust. Show source and as-of time on every number, with charts and tables that make curves and ARBs easy to read.

  • Work with the people who use it. Pair with designers, product and SMEs, and talk to traders to see where the experience breaks.

  • Use AI to build faster. Prototype with Claude Code, write tests that keep pace, and help raise our bar on testing beyond the UI.

What you bring

  • Proven experience building production web applications across front end and back end.

  • Strong TypeScript, React.

  • Experience with real-time UIs: streaming (SSE or WebSockets), optimistic updates and resilient reconnects.

  • Backend skills in Node.js or Python, with Postgres and API design (REST, tRPC or GraphQL).

  • A product eye: you sweat latency, empty states and the detail of a chart.

  • Good testing habits: unit, integration and end-to-end.

Nice to have

  • Built UI for LLM products or integrated with an agent backend.

  • Data visualisation for time series or financial data.

  • Design systems and monorepos (Nx, Storybook).

  • Microsoft Teams or Office add-in development.

Our stack for this team

TypeScript · React · tRPC · Kotlin · Postgres · Redis · Python · AWS

Why Join Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded.

• Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company

• $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment

• Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale

• Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence

• Top-tier tools and technology to support your success

What's the Culture Like at Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.

The Sparta Code

Understanding is non-negotiable

Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning.

The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.

Ask for forgiveness, not for permission

Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not.

90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.

Fall in love with the problem

The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to.

Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.

It's your fault. Lucky you.

If it's on you, it's in your control.

True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.

Conflict is a gift

Honesty is an expression of care.

Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

We are determined that no-one will ever receive less favourable treatment on the grounds of gender, age, disability, religion, belief, sexual orientation, marital status, race, veteran status or any basis covered by appropriate law.

jobs.description:
Research Engineer, Agents

About Boltz

Boltz is a public benefit company building the next generation of AI-powered molecular modeling tools to make biology programmable and accelerate drug discovery, while keeping frontier capabilities broadly accessible.

Boltz was founded by former MIT scientists who created Boltz-1, the first fully commercially available open-source model to approach AlphaFold 3-level accuracy in predicting the 3D structure of biomolecular complexes.

We focus on two things:

  • Foundation models. Our open models, Boltz-1, Boltz-2 and BoltzGen, are trusted by 100,000+ scientists across biotech and academia, and used in programs at every Top 20 pharma as well as leading agrichemical and industrial research organizations. Our latest proprietary foundation models power our products and the custom models we build with partners.

  • Boltz Lab and the Boltz API. Our products run our latest models, design pipelines (BoltzMol for small molecules, BoltzProt for protein design) and agents as reliable, production-grade tools built around real chemistry and biology workflows. Teams start from a target and a hypothesis, then generate, evaluate, and rank candidate molecules in Boltz Lab, run our models from their own code and agents through the Boltz API, or deploy them inside their own environment.

The two feed each other: our open releases earn scientific credibility and community insight, and our products turn our full range of models into real impact for partners including Pfizer, Takeda, GSK, Bristol Myers Squibb and DSM-Firmenich.

You can read more about our mission, research and product vision in our manifesto.

 

About the role
As a Research Engineer (Agents), you will build and own the agent harnesses behind research at Boltz. You will design them for our scientific and research use cases, including agentic research pipelines and researcher tooling, and scale them to run on our cluster.
You will be part of Research Engineering and work with researchers across our teams.
This role is ideal for a strong systems engineer who has built agent systems, has sharp intuitions for the capabilities and limitations of current frontier LLMs, both open- and closed-source, and is rigorous about the correctness of agent output. You do not need an ML research background.

What you’ll do

  • Design and build agent harnesses for research: tool use, orchestration, and context and state management.

  • Work with researchers to build agentic pipelines and tooling for their work, and make them reusable across teams.

  • Scale these harnesses to support large agent swarms on our cluster.

  • Build observability, verification and cost control for large agent runs.

  • Evaluate agent setups rigorously, and keep our harnesses current as frontier LLMs evolve.

About you

Minimum Requirements

  • Strong software engineering experience, including distributed systems or infrastructure that runs many long-running jobs in parallel and handles failures.

  • Experience building agent systems or harnesses (tool use, orchestration, context and state management, evaluation) that you can discuss in depth.

  • Good judgment about the capabilities and failure modes of frontier LLMs, and about keeping agent-produced work correct and maintainable.

  • A track record of building tools that were widely adopted by researchers or engineers.

Preferred Requirements

  • Experience developing open-source agent harnesses (e.g. Pi, Codex, DSH) or extending existing ones (e.g. Claude Code).

  • Understanding of LLM architectures, and experience fine-tuning LLMs with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or reinforcement learning (e.g. RLHF, RLVR, GRPO).

  • Background in NLP or information retrieval, such as search, ranking, embeddings, vector search or retrieval-augmented generation.

  • Experience running workloads on a shared compute cluster or cloud infrastructure (e.g. Kubernetes).

  • Exposure to scientific research workflows.

  • Experience using Boltz models.

 

What we offer

  • Work alongside one of the most talent-dense teams in the field.

  • Significant ownership and independence, with responsibility for driving projects from concept to deployment.

  • Highly competitive salary with meaningful equity in a public benefit company.

  • Benefits:

    • 25 days plus bank holidays a year

    • Annual team offsite trip

    • Private healthcare (BUPA), covering pre-existing conditions

    • Pension program

    • Paid parental leave

    • Wellhub gym membership

    • Free lunch every day

    • Travel expenses

 

How we hire

  1. Initial screen with a member of the Talent team

  2. Diagnosis interview: work through a degraded training run with us (no manual coding test)

  3. Onsite in London or virtual onsite with the team

  4. Offer + Onboarding

 

Our commitment

Boltz is committed to building a diverse team and an inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds. If you need any adjustments during the hiring process, tell us and we'll make it work.
